title: Wellness Warriors — School Holiday Health Campaign
objective: Drive family health check-ups and preventative wellness during school holidays by positioning healthcare as a summer wellness ritual for busy parents.
target_audience: Parents aged 28–48 with school-age children; dual-income households in Central, East, and North Singapore.
key_activities: Launch 'Wellness Wednesday' social series (8 carousel posts + 6 reels on preventative health habits)
Partner with 3 micro-influencers (parenting/lifestyle, 50k–150k followers) for authentic family wellness stories
Paid Meta campaign targeting parent interest clusters with dynamic creative (rational: health savings angle; emotional: family peace-of-mind; disruptive: 'holiday wellness' novelty)
Weekly community management + Q&A live sessions on health questions
Lead capture via bookable appointment link + SMS nurture sequence
why_now: School holidays (June 22 – July 28) create a fixed window when parents have flexibility and mental space for family health decisions. Family wellness is a natural seasonal narrative—capitalise before August back-to-school anxiety shifts focus.
deliverables: 8 carousel posts (wellness habit breakdowns: hydration, sleep, movement, nutrition)
6 reels (30–45s, mobile-first, in-language captions: parenting + health mashups)
3 influencer partnership videos (30–60s, authentic family wellness moments)
1 appointment landing page + SMS nurture sequence (5 messages over 3 weeks)
Daily community management (8–17:00 SG time, Sat/Sun 10–14:00)
Weekly performance dashboard (reach, engagement, lead quality, cost-per-booking)

title: Summer Health Check-In Lab — Pop-Up Wellness Activation
objective: Create a frictionless, Instagram-worthy health screening experience that drives trial, builds brand affinity, and generates qualified patient data during school holidays.
target_audience: Health-conscious urban professionals and parents (25–55), Instagram-active, mid-to-upper middle income, concentrated in CBD and East Coast mall clusters.
key_activities: 2-week pop-up activation at 2 high-footfall malls (Orchard Central, East Coast Mall); 3-station micro-clinic setup (BP/BMI screening, wellness risk assessment, skin analysis via AI camera)
Branded photo booth with on-the-spot prints + Instagram frame (social wall incentive)
Free wellness consultation + personalised follow-up email with next-steps pathway
Daily 15–30s video reels of guests + wellness moments; UGC hashtag campaign (#MyWellnessCheckIn)
Sampling of branded wellness products (vitamin packs, face masks) to drive trial + word-of-mouth
kpis: 750+ footfall across 2 sites; conversion to screening ≥60%
420 qualified patient leads (appointment bookings within 30 days)
why_now: July school holidays = family mall footfall surge. Parents actively seeking summer activities + health consciousness peaks in wellness season. Pop-ups are high-intent touchpoints that convert faster than digital-only.
deliverables: Venue hire + setup/breakdown for 2 malls (14 days each; AV, signage, furniture, staffing)
Branded photo booth (backdrop design + printing; 2 units)
AI wellness station (skin/health risk assessment software integration; 1-week lease)
Daily content (10 reels, 20 stills over 14 days; edited, 48-hour turnaround)
Event merchandise (300 branded tote bags + 500 vitamin sample packs)
Lead capture system + post-event email nurture sequence (7 emails over 3 weeks)
Final event report (footfall, lead quality, ROI per site) + UGC gallery

title: Mental Wellness @ Work — B2B Corporate Wellness Campaign
objective: Generate qualified B2B leads (HR/wellness managers at mid-market corporates) by positioning mental wellness as a Q3 investment priority, tying to back-to-work stress recovery post-holidays.
target_audience: HR managers, wellness coordinators, office managers at mid-market companies (100–1,000 employees) in Singapore; secondary: multinational HQs and professional services (law, finance, consulting).
key_activities: Paid LinkedIn campaign targeting HR decision-makers with 3 ad angles: ROI on wellness spend, employee retention impact, post-holiday stress recovery
Content pillar: 'Wellness ROI Playbook' (downloadable PDF) + 4 thought-leadership articles (mental health trends, corporate burnout stats, July recovery strategy)
Webinar series (2 × 30min): 'Mental Wellness as a Retention Tool' + 'Building a Back-to-Work Recovery Programme' with guest speaker (corporate wellness expert)
Email nurture sequence (6-touch, 4-week cycle) with case study + ROI calculator
Retargeting to webinar attendees with demo offer
kpis: 180 qualified leads (lead score ≥60; HR decision-makers, company size + budget signals confirmed)
why_now: Post-school holidays (late July) marks the start of Q3 budgeting cycle and 'back-to-work' stress peaks. B2B wellness decision-making clusters in Q3 (procurement cycle + headcount planning). Mental health gains visibility post-summer slump.
deliverables: LinkedIn paid campaign (3 ad creatives, 4-week run, audience segmentation by company size/role)
Downloadable wellness ROI playbook (PDF, 12 pages, branded, with calculator)
4 thought-leadership articles (800 words each, SEO-optimised, published on owned blog + synced to LinkedIn)
2 webinars (30-min each, slides, speaker prep, live moderation, Q&A recording)
Email nurture sequence (6 emails, 4-week cadence, personalisation by company size)
Retargeting pixel + dynamic ads for webinar attendees (2-week window)
Lead scoring & qualification summary (weekly report, lead list with MONI flags)

title: Telehealth Summer Sprint — Youth Digital Health Campaign
objective: Acquire new young patients (18–34) for telehealth services by leveraging school holidays + summer travel as high-intent moments for on-demand healthcare access.
target_audience: Urban Gen-Z & millennials (18–34), digitally native, Instagram/TikTok primary, students and young professionals, cost-conscious, health-aware but time-poor.
key_activities: TikTok + Instagram Reels content series: 12 short-form videos (15–30s) showing relatable health scenarios (acne breakouts, travel health anxiety, hangover remedies, period pain management) solved via telehealth; humorous, peer-to-peer tone
Partner with 4 mid-tier creators (Gen-Z health/lifestyle, 80k–300k followers) for authentic 'I tried telehealth' content + discount codes
Paid TikTok + Instagram campaign with dynamic product ads (appointment booking CTA) + retargeting (website visitors, video viewers)
SMS/WhatsApp nurture: 3-touch sequence offering first-appointment discount + testimonial snippets
In-app chat QA series answering common health questions (anxiety-reducing, trust-building)
kpis: 850 new telehealth app downloads / sign-ups (cost-per-install ≤ S$8)
18% CTR on TikTok product ads; 6.2% Instagram ROAS
42% of bookings from paid channels (attribution via UTM)
why_now: July school holidays + university break = peak mobile usage + travel (high telehealth demand: pharmacies closed, doctor access limited). Youth wellness trends favour on-demand, stigma-free services. Summer content consumption highest on TikTok.
deliverables: 12 TikTok/Reels videos (15–30s, scripted, produced, captions, music licensing)
4 creator partnership videos (organic-style, 30–60s, discount codes embedded)
TikTok paid campaign (3 product ad variants, 14-day run, retargeting pixel setup)
Instagram paid campaign (carousel + dynamic ads, 14-day run)
SMS/WhatsApp nurture sequence (3 messages over 7 days, personalisation by booking stage)
In-app Q&A content (8 pre-recorded short answers to common health Qs; 30–60s clips)
Daily social management (comments, DMs, UGC reposting, 09:00–22:00)
Campaign performance dashboard (downloads, bookings, ROAS, cost-per-acquisition by channel)

title: Healing Moments — Medical Clinic Rebranding + Launch Campaign
objective: Reposition a traditional medical clinic as a modern, patient-centric wellness destination; drive awareness and trial during a physical clinic refresh + rebrand launch.
target_audience: Suburban families (30–55), health-conscious professionals (25–45), existing patient base (retention focus), neighbourhood residents within 2km radius of clinic location.
key_activities: Full rebrand identity system (logo, colour palette, typography, brand guidelines) + brand story articulation ('from clinical to caring')
Clinic refresh photography + brand film (2–3min cinematic walkthrough showing modern spaces, warm staff, patient testimonials)
Launch event (80–120 guests: existing patients, neighbours, local influencers, media; 2-hour open house with health screening, light refreshments, exclusive opening discounts)
Post-launch social campaign (8 weeks: behind-the-scenes reels, staff spotlights, patient stories, health tips tied to clinic services)
Integrated PR outreach (local lifestyle media, neighbourhood newsletters, Google My Business overhaul)
kpis: 120 launch event attendees; ≥60% conversion to new patient appointments within 30 days
2,200 new social followers (pre-launch to 12 weeks post)
45% increase in new patient enquiries week-on-week post-launch (baseline: 4 weeks pre-launch)
Google My Business rating ≥ 4.7 stars with ≥80 new reviews
why_now: July school holidays lower patient flow but create a natural 'reset' moment for clinic closures/refresh. Late July launch = August back-to-work + school reopening drives health appointment-booking behaviour. Rebranding gains momentum in slower season.
deliverables: Rebrand identity system (logo 5 variants, colour palette, typography specs, 40-page brand guidelines)
Brand story document + key messaging framework (for staff + all communications)
Clinic photography session (120+ branded images: spaces, staff portraits, patient moments; 2-day shoot)
Brand film (2.5 min cinematic walkthrough + testimonials; edited, colour-graded, 3 cuts: social, website, launch event)
Launch event (venue hire, AV setup, catering for 120, event signage, staff training, photography/video coverage, post-event recap reel)
8-week social campaign (16 reels, 24 carousel posts, staff spotlights, health tips, patient stories; daily posting)
Google My Business overhaul (photos, verified info, service categories, opening hours, CTA setup)
PR outreach kit (press release, media list, localised pitches, follow-up support)
Post-launch report (event attendance, new patients acquired, social growth, media reach, appointment lift)
